quest.title: Hearken, Ye Who Have Returned
quest.description: Natlan's very first leader, the mighty first Pyro Archon Xbalanque, has appeared before all in a form and manner beyond imagination...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Guide to Contention x5, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Okay, this should be far enough. Sorry for making you walk all this way. I am Natlan's current leader and Pyro Archon, Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Lord Xbalanque. I, um... I said I was inviting you for a chat, but to be perfectly honest, this is also my first time doing something like this, so... I don't even know where to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Oh no... He doesn't sound too impressed...)

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: You mean you've never hosted a long-dead guy on his first trip home before? No worries, it's a first for me too.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: ...I didn't realize you also had a sense of humor.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Wait, really? Hang on, I think I just realized something.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: —You're telling me that neither you nor your companions know that I, Xbalanque, was totally hilarious?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: All the woven scrolls regarding your life depict you as a wise and upright person. According to legends, you also used the divine throne to negotiate with the Ruler of Death, establishing the set of rules unique to Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: As for your sense of humor... no sources ever touched upon it. Maybe it's better to say that we know even less about you than we expected.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I see... In that case, allow me to re-introduce myself. I am the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque. You may call me "Dear Beloved Sun," or just "Lanque" for short.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, talk about being overly familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Keep your voice down! Are you looking to get smacked...?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: And these two are?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #Allow me to introduce {NICKNAME} and Paimon. They are important friends of Natlan, and our companions, great heroes who helped us defeat the Abyss for good.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. I was about to say, why did a child follow us all the way here... Ha! Though you could say the same for me. And judging by your expression, that's exactly what you're saying.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: And there's where you'd be wrong. This body belongs to a child of present-day Natlan. I'm only possessing it temporarily.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I see. Your physical body couldn't be revived, so you had to borrow someone else's... But what about the original owner? Is he... okay?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: No need to worry. My existence has not affected this child in any way. This body's original occupant is currently experiencing a fantastic dream.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I have my own plans. And as for my reasoning, you'll find out soon enough.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Alas, this borrowed body is a bit lacking when it comes to exercise, and hasn't really trained any aspect. I tried my best at the tournament, but could only get so far given my physical limitations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that explains why you couldn't make a deep run... You're not used to this body, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I wish that was the only problem! I'm simply unable to do a lot of larger movements. Oh, and my usual climbing and jumping motions aren't exactly suited for him, either.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Also, you've got to be twice as careful in a borrowed body. If I pushed him too hard and got him hurt, I'd be no better than a criminal! I could never do anything like that.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Indeed. Still, the great shaman Citlali learned about your impending resurrection from the Wayob, but we still don't know why you've returned.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Oh? Is it time to get serious, then? Alright, serious mode activated!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Ahem. In any case, you've already touched on the topic.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I did indeed strike a deal with the Ruler of Death. She once asked me why I prayed for her power as a mere mortal, and why I yearned to save a nation in peril.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I convinced her with the promise of perpetual existence and the everlasting flame of life. So she shared her strength with me, and allowed Natlan to operate under brand new rules.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I told her that the plan would be a grand, long-term one. One in which victory would not come for some time — certainly not within a mortal lifespan. Still, I knew that someone else would bring it home.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: She assented to my request, and became an observer of our tale. Seeing her interest, I also asked that I, as the one who laid the foundation, be granted an opportunity to see the new world with my own eyes if we actually did manage to triumph in the far future.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, your return is a special favor granted by the Ruler of Death.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: More like a bet I made with her. Even gods have things that pique their interest. I bet correctly on the outcome of this war, so this trip is my reward.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: How do you feel about the Natlan of today? Does it meet your expectations?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Oh, I like it a lot. Could you tell me more, by the way? I'd love to know how you managed to win the war.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: ...As you know, ours was an exceedingly grand, long-term plan.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I will skip over the most ancient parts, and start with what I know — the battle from five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The disaster struck suddenly, and Natlan was engulfed in darkness. Our land and faith were both shattered, and everyone believed that our nation's end was nigh.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But even when thrust into battle against the Abyss, fate, and the passage of time, our heroes did not give up hope of victory. We each shouldered our heavy duty using the power that you left behind.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: All the Pyro Archons in the last five hundred years have devoted their lives to banishing the Abyss, rebuilding our tribes and faith, and uniting the people as one.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: As for me, I decided to head five hundred years into the future — that is, the present — so I might finally bring together our people's resolve, which has stood firm for thousands of years, and fight for our final victory.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Of course, I had prepared for the worst. That I would awaken to naught but monsters, corpses, and ruins where our nation once stood.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Had that happened, there would only have been one thing left for me to do: fulfill my final duty as a warrior, and then, witness the end of the world helplessly.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Still, the outcome proved that our faith was not misplaced. This victory, and the miracle that it created, is the greatest reward for all who gave everything to protect our realm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, had anything gone wrong, whether in the past or in the now...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I've always believed you to be shrewd. Surely, such a quality was needed to bargain with the Ruler of Death, and win so much for us in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Natlan was only able to overcome this crisis with your help.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: ...All these millennia later, and the people of Natlan have finally achieved victory over fate.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: If future generations will call me the one who created the rules and initiated the plan, then you are the one who inherited those rules, the final executor of the plan, the one who created a miracle.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Beginnings and endings, creation and change... Mavuika, you truly are a remarkable leader. It is my honor to have met you.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Please, you're too modest. Rather, it is our honor to welcome you back to this world.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Ah, and that's the perfect segue to something that you should know.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: You see... Uh, you don't have to worry too much about my second life, since I'll only be here for a single day. Like... from sunrise to sunset.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: A single day!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But the day... is almost over!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Haha, that's why I said you won't have to worry too much about the boy this body actually belongs to. I'll be long gone by this time tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Besides, no one ever said I was actually going to return and stick around for years and years, right? This is just a short little outing back home, so I can see some of my compatriots again.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Still, I've gotta say, it has not been an easy trip. After being resurrected, I woke up in the home of a normal boy, and wanted to take a quick dip to relax, only to have my trouser leg snagged by a fishing line that came outta nowhere...

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: And once I finally made it to shore, I decided to take a stroll and see the sights, only to step into a trap along the way! Beats me who'd put a trap out there, and there wasn't even anybody around to check it!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Thankfully, the bottom was pretty soft, so I lay down and took a nap before getting up to continue on my merry way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (This is so embarrassing...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I swear, with friends like these...)

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: After countless trials and tribulations, I finally managed to sign up for the tournament, but then I ran into a girl who claimed to be a fitness coach. She insisted that my muscles weren't up to snuff and made me do twice as many warm-up exercises as everyone else...

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: *sigh* You guys in the future sure have it rough.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Well, then... What's next for you?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Aw, what a great question. I was just about to get to that. You're a pretty considerate gal!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: So, I do have a small wish that I haven't been able to fulfill.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I managed to participate in the Pilgrimage, but alas, my potential is restricted by this form. It sure would be nice if I could show everyone what I can actually do...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Why is he stealing glances at us like that...

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Well, now that I've said it, care to help an old man out, hero?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Okay... So, uh, what are you capable of?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Ahem! See, I was also quite the formidable warrior in my time — surely, a match for Mavuika. I mean, I was the first Pyro Archon, after all. I could shake the cliffs with a single punch, scale mountains with a single leap.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Very formidable indeed. So, you'd like to spar with me?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Using your current body? Will he be able to handle it?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll find a suitable location for our duel, and a way to keep this body safe.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: The first sun... the ardent sun. This star is a flame, burning with a passion that will consume all.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: From the moment I first saw you, I knew you to be a true warrior, just like me.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Surely, you shall not refuse me this battle — O inheritor of my Ancient Name, the burning sun, "Kion{RUBY#[D]Leader}gozi" Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I accept.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Brilliant. In that case, let us free ourselves from mortal shape. Let the ancient souls guide you to the true arena of duels!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What... is this place?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: ...Is this a temple of the spirit?

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: This is the land of the sun, created by my soul. Only the sun and those blessed by it can survive here.

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: Me, you, you, and you. The sun, the other sun, Blessed One-One, and Blessed One-Two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've been... blessed by the sun?

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: The sun will remember the most virtuous stars. You are hope itself — the most radiant, most important friends we could have.

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: We have invited you here, so you may witness the clash of suns.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I see... We've manifested in an almost fully spiritual, consciousness-like form, removing the limits of our flesh.

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: As I said, I knew you to be a born warrior the moment I laid eyes on you. But there are two forms of human strength: that of the body, and of the spirit.

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: The great Xbalanque, impressed upon a child's body, found less than a third of his original strength available to him. In that form, I'd lost my strength of body.

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: But here, we meet as our true spiritual selves. In this place, even a child may shake heaven and earth due to the great soul within.

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: What makes a true hero? Someone strong of body? Or strong of mind? Or... must one be strong in both to surpass human limits?

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: Which of these are you, Mavuika?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Ha. Well said, Xbalanque. Let us prove our mastery of both strengths through this battle — to Natlan, to each other, and to the rest of the world.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You and I both know we'll never meet a better-matched opponent.

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: Indeed. That's exactly what I've always wanted.

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: As a citizen of Natlan, as the Pyro Archon, as an opponent from across the millennia and a friend whom you never had the chance to meet...

response.speaker: Xbalanque
response.text: Let us have a fair and honorable duel!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It was a great fight.

talks.objective: Leave the Temple of the Spirit
Go for a ride with everyone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We made it! Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Woo! Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Thank you, Mavuika. This has been a wonderful trip.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Lovely things are meant to be shared, after all. It's the least we could do for our friend.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I'll admit, I didn't expect people several thousand years in the future to see me as a friend.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Not that I'm complaining. This old man's had a great day today. Thank you, dear friends.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I can still remember how nervous you looked when you saw me for the first time, Mavuika... I'll cherish that memory.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Oh. Is it almost time?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Yes, it is.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Thank you for coming back to see us. This meeting means a lot to me as well.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Mhm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Well, time to go. Don't forget to lead a happy life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, already? Paimon's gonna miss you. See ya later, Xbalanque!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Enjoy your life in the Night Kingdom, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, he closed his eyes... Did he fall asleep?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Mhm. I can no longer sense Xbalanque's soul.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Well, it's gotten quite late, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Thank you for accompanying me this whole time. Let's hurry back, you must be starving.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There'll be a victory feast tonight, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes. After the end of the Pilgrimage, we hold a banquet to congratulate the champion of the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: There will be good food and plenty of it — You guys are gonna love it. Mausau should be there, too — I'll bring him over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think there'll still be any food left over for us? It's kinda late and all...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'm sure the feast has already started, but don't worry, I'm sure Iansan will save some for us.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: She's very reliable. Leaving the tournament planning to her was a smart move.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, so she probably figured that we'd be gone a long time...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yeah, I told her as much too.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Ah, seems like they've prepared the thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What thing?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: See that row of braziers over there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's what they are! They haven't been lit, so Paimon totally thought they were something else.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Here, watch this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! They're beautiful...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Were they left for the three of us?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: This particular kind of brazier is called a "signal flame," and is reserved for those coming back late at night. The others set up an entire path using these signal flames to await our return.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Those returning to the tribes must light them with their own hands. The flames will illuminate the path ahead, and show the tribe that the person has made it back.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "Even if you're surrounded by darkness, never forget — your friends wait for you in the distant light." Remember that feeling when the exhaustion of your journey creeps up on you.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Archon, {NICKNAME}, Paimon! You were really gone a long time. We've already started grilling the meat.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We had a long talk with Lord Xbalanque. It was pretty time-consuming.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Did it all go well?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: More than well. Xbalanque... He is a very good man. He far surpassed even my expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The people at the feast all gather around you, Paimon, and Mavuika. Mavuika gestures for everyone to move over and sit down at the drinking table, before beginning to tell the story...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: She reveals everything without reservation, holding nothing back and hiding no secrets. As a part of the deal made millennia ago, the ancient sun could only rise again for one day. Still it was enough time for her to recount all the people's achievements and hard work to him.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As night fell, the sun disappeared once more. She returned with joy in her heart, and a child of the tribes on her back.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The sun arose in that child's dream, and quietly set in his deep sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: So the only reason Lord Xbalanque didn't win the tournament is because he was limited by the physical body he was in...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right, but don't feel disappointed on his behalf — he himself was not upset about that turn of events.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: He had many revelations during this journey. And as he said, strength of mind is as important as the strength of the body. He realized that after failing to make it to the final 32.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No matter how many times Paimon hears it, it's still so funny to think that Xbalanque didn't even make it that far...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You'd have never expected to hear those words next to each other.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Strong in both body and mind, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'd say our champion, Kinich, fits the bill, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Indeed. Everyone, let's raise our cups — let's celebrate our champion!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Kinich, you've proven yourself a true warrior and athlete. Congratulations on your triumph in the Pilgrimage!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: A toast to our champion!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Cheers!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, look, the kid's awake!

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: Uhh... Huh? Where am I...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hello, Mausau. You're awake. This is the celebration feast for the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. You participated in the tournament, too.

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: Huh? M—Me?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: It's a long story.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: It's so long, even my lowly servant couldn't manage to give a simple summary, heh!

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: I see... I remember... Lord Xbalanque, our Archon, Mavuika, and... the Pilgrimage.

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: I feel like I dreamed a very long dream. I was super strong in that dream, too... I could jump up onto the roof with one leap, and I could climb, fly, and glide...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It wasn't a dream. Your body did go through all the motions of the tournament. You are already an outstanding contestant.

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: I... I'm a... contestant?

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: You know, Mom and Dad always say that my health isn't the best, and I might not be able to do all the things everyone else can... But right now, I feel like I can fly!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Like Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: Yeah! I feel amazing... It's like I'm filled with power from head to toe. I... I wanna feel like this next time, too!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Then go and train hard, then come back next year and show us what you've got.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yeah! As long as you put in the work, you'll do great, I know it! That's how it is for all of us.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Yes. You'll turn out to be a truly beautiful vegetable, I am sure of it.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Vegetable...

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: Yeah, I will!

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: Oh, but the Pilgrimage was only half of the dream. I think, after that... I somehow got into a fight...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Really? Against who?

dialogues.speaker: Mausau
dialogues.text: I think it was... our Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That wasn't a dream, either. I did have a duel with Xbalanque.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Haha, I was hoping to save this until later, but since we're already on this topic, I've got another piece of good news to share.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Namely, that we crowned another champion today. Lord Xbalanque and I engaged in an all-out duel, as worthy rivals from across the millennia.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In the end, I won by the slimmest of margins, defeating our legendary hero.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Woooooow!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I can't believe it. You beat THE Xbalanque?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: This is no lie, and I have our best friend here to back me up. You were the arbiter for our duel, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: *clears throat*...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mavuika is right. Paimon and I witnessed her victory with our own eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Amazing! What an achievement!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: C'mon, everyone, let's have another toast, for our Archon this time!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Very well. Acknowledge my victory, recognize my valor, and drink this wine of victory for me!

dialogues.speaker: Ecstatic Audience Members
dialogues.text: Woo-hoo! Yay!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Phew.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Today's been a super long and exciting day, yeah?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yeah. It's been quite some time since I've done so much in a day, or felt that it's gone on for so long.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But you've also got a sense of accomplishment to match, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh right, Mavuika, {NICKNAME} said there was something to ask you.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I was just thinking... You were fighting Xbalanque for such a long time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you ever falter, or wonder if you might lose to him, even for a second?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No. In battle, there is no time for that. So, it never crossed my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Huh? That's the same answer as last time...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...How come she knew what I was thinking?)

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The night is still young. Cheers.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Helmets on, sit tight, and don't fall!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Is this a board you can use to ride on the water? And you can stick it to the back of vehicles, too! Genius!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is Mavuika's flamestrider! Oh, we call that board a "surfboard"!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Haha, you learn something new all the time!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Playing with this stuff is part of everyday life, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We're livin' good!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Ah, I wonder if I would've ever become Pyro Archon if we had had these gadgets around back then. I might've had too a bit much fun with them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? That would be terrible!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Agreed! Good thing they were only invented after I died, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hahaha, looks like I really am better after all, for becoming Pyro Archon even with all this temptation around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Point Mavuika!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The hands of our friends at the Children of Echoes are as skilled as ever. They were already famed in your era, right? This bike was built by their most talented artisan in this age.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, we just passed them by.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Sweet!

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Is that Ochkanatlan? Ahh... Sure brings back memories.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! That was built in your time, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It's long become a landmark. Very popular with tourists, so I hear — they think it's a lovely place.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Is that so? So that's how you all see it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks so too! It's especially stunning if you look at it from a Spiritway.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The stories of the past become things people aspire to in the future. It's just like what they say — the apex reached by those who came before will become the everyday goals of those who come after. Everything is constantly changing for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: That's good. That's how it should be. I'll bring those words back to the Night Kingdom, and share them with everyone there.
